objectives.description: Apply the shared per-phase procedure to the 17 declared files
objectives.note: All 17 files treated; zero remaining dead-command tokens under the measurement command restricted to this tranche's file list. index-entries.json line_count entries hand-corrected for batch-gate-stage.md (163->164); all other touched files' line counts were unaffected (inline text substitutions of equal line count) and verified unchanged against their declared entries.

objectives.description: system-overview.md: reword the dead-command half only, leave the record-versioning phrasing untouched
objectives.note: 'the standalone `/research`, `/plan`, `/implement` commands ... that used to occupy Layers 1-2 ... have been deleted' -> 'the standalone research, plan, and implement commands ... that used to occupy Layers 1-2 ... have been deleted'. Only the backtick-wrapped slash-command tokens were dropped (phase names substituted); 'Superseded note', 'used to occupy', and 'have been deleted' are preserved verbatim per the explicit Non-Goal.

objectives.description: The two .json schema files (index.schema.json, schemas/errors-schema.json) and orchestrator-handoff-schema.json: class-3-vs-class-2 check
objectives.note: VERDICT for all three: class 2 (prose about the system inside a JSON description/examples field), not class 3. index.schema.json's `examples: [["/implement", "/plan"]]` for the context-index `load_when.commands` field, and core/context/README.md's matching worked example `{ "commands": ["/research", "/implement"] }`, were both illustrating a currently-invalid configuration -- every live `commands` array in agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json is empty (grep-confirmed), so holding up dead commands as the canonical example was actively misleading, not a harmless fixture. Both corrected to a live-command example (`["/revise", "/task"]`). errors-schema.json's `command` field description example ('e.g. /implement, /plan') and orchestrator-handoff-schema.json's 'a standalone /research, /plan, or /implement invocation' phrase were both ordinary class-2 prose claims and reworded to phase-dispatch framing; neither is detected or matched by code (unlike lint-dead-command-recommendations.sh's class-3 strings), so neither qualifies for the class-3 leave-alone treatment despite being JSON.

objectives.description: manifest-routing-schema.md: dead-command tokens reworded inside a record-versioning-heavy paragraph
objectives.note: The paragraph ('Collapsed model (post routing-ladder-collapse)') is itself squarely in the record-versioning-exempt class (a dated architectural-change explanation, heavy with 'now-removed'/'no longer exists'/'retired outright'), same as revise.md's companion exemption class named in the plan's Non-Goals ('confirmed advisory-tier by the live gate, owned by a completed taxonomy/lint/hook lineage'). Only the bare dead-command tokens ('`/research`, `/plan`, `/implement`' -> 'research, plan, and implement') were reworded; the surrounding versioning language ('now-deleted', 'once those commands were deleted', 'retired outright, not migrated', 'no longer exists') was left exactly as-is, mirroring the system-overview.md treatment in objective 2.

objectives.description: command-template.md: worked example heading using a dead command as illustration
objectives.note: '## Example: /research Command' -> '## Example: Research-Phase Checkpoint Flow'. The body's status strings ('researching'/'researched') are phase-status markers, not command tokens, and were left unchanged; they do not match the measurement pattern and are substantively accurate regardless of the dead command name.
